topics.title: Thermodynamic terms: system, state and internal energy

concepts.learning_objective: Classify a system as open, closed or isolated from its exchange of energy and matter.
Distinguish state functions from path-dependent quantities such as heat and work.
Apply the first law, delta U = q + w, with the IUPAC sign convention.

topics.title: Applications: work, enthalpy and heat capacity

concepts.learning_objective: Calculate pressure-volume work for expansion against a constant external pressure and for free expansion.
Relate delta H and delta U through delta H = delta U + delta n(g) RT.
Distinguish extensive and intensive properties and use heat capacities, including Cp - Cv = R.

topics.title: Measurement of delta U and delta H: calorimetry

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why a bomb calorimeter measures delta U and calculate it from a temperature rise.
Explain that heat measured at constant pressure equals delta H and relate delta H to delta U for combustion.

topics.title: Enthalpy change of a reaction and Hess's law

concepts.learning_objective: Identify formation reactions and calculate reaction enthalpy from standard enthalpies of formation.
Interpret enthalpies of fusion and vaporisation and use them in enthalpy calculations.
Apply Hess's law by adding, reversing and scaling thermochemical equations.

topics.title: Enthalpies for different types of reactions

concepts.learning_objective: Use bond and atomization enthalpies to estimate reaction enthalpies for gaseous reactions.
Define lattice enthalpy and calculate it from a Born-Haber cycle.
Relate enthalpy of solution to lattice enthalpy and enthalpy of hydration.
Use the entropy criterion of spontaneity and calculate the entropy change of the surroundings.
Predict spontaneity from delta G = delta H - T delta S and the effect of temperature.
State the third law of thermodynamics and its use for absolute entropies.
State that delta r G = 0 at equilibrium and distinguish delta r G from the standard value.
Use delta r G standard = -2.303 RT log K to relate standard Gibbs energy and the equilibrium constant.
